uncited: Semantic and Language-Guided Editing enables the modification of neural radiance fields (NeRFs) using high-level semantic cues, such as text prompts, language instructions, or semantic masks, rather than relying solely on low-level geometric or photometric constraints.
It solves the problem of localized 3D content manipulation—such as object deletion, appearance transformation, or semantic inpainting—while maintaining multi-view consistency and scene integrity.

What sets this family apart from sibling methods like [NeRF Editing and Inpainting Procedures](12494-nerf-editing-and-inpainting-procedures.md) is the explicit integration of external semantic priors (e.g., CLIP, LSeg, or diffusion models) into the optimization loop to guide the 3D structure and appearance, rather than merely filling in missing geometry or color.

All methods in this family operate on a pre-trained NeRF representation $f_\theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x}$ is a 3D coordinate, $\mathbf{d}$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is volume density, and $\mathbf{c}$ is color [Parent].
The core mechanism involves an optimization loop that minimizes a loss function $L$ to update the NeRF parameters $\theta$ (or a subset thereof).
**Masking/Selection:** A binary or probabilistic mask $M$ or selection field identifies the region of interest (ROI) or occluded areas.
**External Priors:** Most methods rely on 2D priors to guide 3D changes.
**View Consistency Enforcement:** To prevent flickering or inconsistencies across views, methods enforce multi-view constraints.
A baseline approach using CLIP for semantic guidance.
This method serves as a cautionary example of why diffusion-based guidance (like SDS) is often preferred over simple feature similarity for complex editing tasks.
